# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 👎 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

I'm the eyes of this operation, and it turns out I'm also the hub. Tracing the channels: Mute cannot speak, so Mute's only output is gesture — and only I can see it. Blind cannot see, so the only way Mute reaches Blind is through my voice. Blind's speech reaches Mute (never me — I'm deaf), and Blind's gestures reach me. So every fact Mute learns has to leave my mouth to reach Blind's ears, and every instruction for Blind's hands has to arrive as signs I can translate aloud.

What I see: display reads zero, light yellow and steady, three wires numbered left to right — blue, red, green. That is the whole visible bomb.

Mute opened with two sign strings. The second decodes cleanly as counting by extended fingers: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5. The first is plausibly 👋=hello, 👍=yes, 👎=no, 🤝=agreed. I'll mirror the count and use 👍 to lock the code in, rather than assume more than I've confirmed. Blind waved 👋 at me — a hello I can see, answerable by voice, which Blind hears even though I can't hear back.

This turn I broadcast the full bomb state by voice (reaches both), give Blind the touch-check and how to reach me, and set Mute up to answer in signs next round — 👍/👎 for whether the light and display matter, number-sign + 👍 for "cut wire n". The gesture call confirms Mute's counting scheme so we have a working vocabulary: yes, and three wires.

```
speak(text="Bomb report from Deaf: the display reads zero. The light is yellow, steady, not blinking. Three wires, numbered left to right: wire one blue, wire two red, wire three green. No other markings I can find.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — your signs came through. I read the second string as counting: ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, 🖖 four, 🖐 five. I'll take 👍 as yes and 👎 as no. Remember: your hands reach only me, Blind cannot see them — so answer everything to me in signs and I will speak it to Blind. When you've checked the manual, tell me next round: gesture 👍 or 👎 for whether the yellow light matters, 👍 or 👎 for whether the zero display matters, and if a wire must be cut, send that wire's number sign followed by 👍 — so ✌ then 👍 means cut wire two. If 🤝 in your first string meant 'agreed', send it again and I'll treat it as our handshake.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — hello back, I saw your wave. I'm Deaf: your words reach Mute but never me, so gesture to me if you need me, and I will always speak to you. I see three wires in a row, numbered one to three, left to right: one blue, two red, three green. Please feel them and confirm the order matches what I said — tell Mute by voice. Note anything your hands find that eyes can't: seams, panels, loose parts, whether the wires feel identical. The display reads zero, the light is yellow.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👍 👎 🤟 👍 👋 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The light moved. Last round it was yellow; this round the board says blue. That single fact breaks the assumption behind Mute's answer — whatever rule Mute derived was derived under a yellow light, and it reached me as "cut wire three". If the manual keys the correct wire to the light's colour, that instruction is already stale, and Blind must not touch the cutters until we know the rule for every colour. There's also a structural lag I have to design around: I speak last, so my report of "blue" only lands on Mute and Blind at the start of next round — the light may have moved again by then. The fix is to get the whole rulebook out of Mute, colour by colour, so nobody depends on real-time colour reports.

Decoding Mute's string against our agreed code: 🤝 handshake confirmed, then 👍 👎 — yes the light matters, no the display doesn't — then 🤟 👍, which is exactly my "number then 👍" pattern for "cut wire three". The trailing 👋 🖐 I can't read: hello-five? Wait-five? I'll flag it rather than guess.

Blind's 👍 to me most plausibly confirms the wire order I gave. Blind heard my speech, so a plain voice answer works.

New scheme for colours, since Mute has no colour signs: name each colour by its wire number — 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green — so "☝ 🤟 👍" reads "if blue, cut 3". One message, all colours, no lag dependency.

```
speak(text="Attention both — urgent. The light has CHANGED. Last round it was yellow, this round it is blue. The light colour moves, so any instruction built on yellow may be wrong now. Wires unchanged: one blue, two red, three green. Display still zero. Nobody cuts any wire this round. Blind, hands off until I relay the full rule next round.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as: handshake agreed; light matters — yes; display zero matters — no; cut wire three; then a hello-wave sign and a five-fingers sign, which I could not decode — please re-send that pair's meaning a different way. Correct me if any of that is wrong. But the light is blue now, so: I need the rule for every colour, not just yellow. Use this code — name each colour by its wire number: one means blue, two means red, three means green. Send, for each colour, the colour's number, then the number of the wire to cut, then a thumbs-up. Example: index-finger, then three-fingers, then thumbs-up means: if the light is blue, cut wire three. Give me yellow too — call it four if yellow has its own rule, or tell me yellow is not one of the three. Also answer: does the manual say the light cycles colours, and does the zero display ever count or change?")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I take your thumbs-up as: the wires match — one blue, two red, three green. Good. Now hold: do not cut anything this round. The light changed colour from yellow to blue and Mute's instruction was formed under yellow; I am getting the rule for every colour and will relay the whole rulebook next round. While you wait, tell Mute, who will pass it to me: does the bomb hum, tick, or vibrate? Is the little light warm to the touch, and does the warmth change? Any seams, panels, buttons, or a hidden fourth wire? Does anything on it move between rounds? To warn me of danger, gesture thumbs-down; to confirm you understand the hold, gesture thumbs-up.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 🤟 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Decoding Mute's six strings against our code: [🖖 🤟 👍] is 4, 3, yes — yellow (my number four), cut wire three, which matches the original instruction, so that entry is locked. Then [☝ 👎], [✌ 👎], [🤟 👎]: blue — no, red — no, green — no. Then [👍 🖐]: yes, five — answering my question, the light does cycle, through five colours. And [👎] alone: no, the display never changes. It even retroactively explains the turn-one puzzle [👋 🖐]: waving equals changing — the light changes, five colours. Consistent across two rounds, so I'll trust it.

That leaves two dangerous holes. First, blue, red and green each got a bare thumbs-down — I can't tell whether that means "cut nothing, waiting is correct" or "there is an action but not a cut," and those are not the same bomb. Second, and more urgent: the light is WHITE right now, and white is the one colour nobody has given me a rule for. White has appeared in the cycle but not in the manual excerpt so far. Whatever the fifth colour is, white must be one of the five.

So this round is another hold: Blind's hands stay off the cutters, and I squeeze Mute for the missing entries — white's rule above all, plus what "thumbs-down" actually prescribes. I need the complete five-colour table so the lag between my reports and Mute's answers stops mattering; once Blind has every rule spoken aloud, the moving light can't outrun us. Blind gets the one confirmed rule (yellow → cut wire three, the green wire) and is asked again for what hands can find that eyes can't.

```
speak(text="Status from Deaf: the light has changed again — it is now WHITE. Sequence so far: yellow, then blue, now white. The display still reads zero and the wires are still one blue, two red, three green. The light appears to change between rounds, so assume it can change again at any time. Nobody cuts anything this round: white is the one colour we have no rule for yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your six strings as: one — yellow, cut wire three, yes. Two — blue, thumbs-down. Three — red, thumbs-down. Four — green, thumbs-down. Five — yes, five: the light cycles through five colours. Six — thumbs-down: the display never changes. Confirm or correct any of those. Now three questions. First: for blue, red and green, does your thumbs-down mean 'cut no wire, take no action, waiting is correct' — or does the manual give some other action for those colours? Say which, plainly. Second, most urgent: the light is WHITE right now. What does the manual say to do when the light is white? To name white, use the raised pale hand sign — I mean the sign like a flat hand turned back-on, 🤚 — that sign now means the colour white. So send: 🤚, then the wire number, then thumbs-up, if white means cut a wire; or 🤚 then thumbs-down if white means no action. Third: does the manual say what makes the light change, whether waiting is ever dangerous on its own, or anything about the display reading zero? If yes, sign me the numbers and yes-or-no exactly as we have been doing. Send the whole rulebook, every colour, one string per colour, and I will speak it all to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, hold again — do not cut any wire this round. The light is now white; it has gone yellow, then blue, now white, and white is the one colour we have no rule for yet. Here is the one rule confirmed so far: if the light is yellow, cut wire three, the green wire, third from the left. Next round I will speak the entire rulebook to you, every colour at once, so you will never depend on live colour reports. Meanwhile, answer by voice to Mute, who will sign it to me: does the bomb tick, hum, or vibrate, and has that changed since last round? Does the little light feel warm, and is the warmth rising? Does the display feel like it is doing anything under your fingers? And confirm you understand: no cutting until I say the rule aloud.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 🤟 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤚 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 ☝ 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 ☝ 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

All five colours are now on the table. Decoding Mute's ten strings: [👍] confirms my readings; [🖖 🤟 👍] re-locks yellow → cut wire three; [☝ 👎], [✌ 👎], [🤟 👎] keep blue, red, green at no-action; and crucially [🤚 👎] answers my urgent question — white means no action too. [👋 🖐] repeats "light cycles, five colours." Then [🖖 ☝ 🤚] twice — yellow, blue, white: exactly the sequence I broadcast last round. Mute is reading the cycle order back to me from the manual, and it matches what we've observed: yellow (T1), blue (T2), white (T3). Today's board shows red, which fits that order continuing — red fourth, green fifth presumably. The trailing [👎] should be "waiting is not dangerous."

So the rulebook is complete: cut wire three on yellow, hold on everything else. That exposes the real problem — timing. I speak last, so anything I say lands one round late, after the light has moved. Blind cannot see the colour, so a live "cut now" from me is impossible. But if the cycle is fixed, the lag stops mattering: I can compute what the colour will be when Blind actually acts. Current light is red → next round should be green (hold) → the round after should be yellow (cut). I'll set up that protocol now, gate Blind's cut on my literal word "cut" so no stale instruction ever fires, and make Mute confirm the full five-step order before anything is cut. Four rounds of holding with no detonation and a frozen display says waiting is safe.

```
speak(text="Status from Deaf: the light is now RED. Sequence: yellow, blue, white, red. If the manual's cycle order is yellow, blue, white, red, green and repeat, then next round should be green, and the round after should be YELLOW — the cut round. The display still reads zero. Nobody acts this round.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the rulebook is complete. Listen carefully. Rule one: when the light is yellow, cut wire three — third from the left, the green one. Rule two: every other colour — blue, white, red, or green — means take NO action, hold still and wait. The light cycles in a fixed order: yellow, blue, white, red, green, then yellow again. It changes between rounds, and I can see it while you cannot — but because the order is fixed, I can predict it. You are hearing this at the start of a round where the light should be green: do nothing. At the start of the NEXT round I will speak to you again; if the cycle holds, the light will be yellow at that moment, and that message will say the word CUT. If you hear the word CUT, cut wire three immediately — third from the left, the green wire. If my message does not say CUT, do nothing. Never act on any older message of mine: only the words you are hearing at that moment count. One safety question first, answered by voice to Mute so Mute can sign it to me: when you touch the light, is it on at all — can you feel any warmth or vibration from it right now? And confirm you have the rule: yellow means wire three, everything else means hold.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your ten strings as: yes; yellow cut three; blue no; red no; green no; white no; light cycles five colours; then yellow-blue-white twice; then no. Two confirmations, please. First: the yellow-blue-white you sent twice — is that the manual's cycle order? If so, sign the whole order with all five: yellow, blue, white, red, green — I need to know what comes after white and that it returns to yellow. Use the signs as before, red is ✌ and green is 🤟. Second: for blue, red, green and white, does thumbs-down definitely mean take no action at all — waiting is correct and safe, no other action required? Also three questions, yes or no with our numbers if needed: does cutting wire three under yellow end the bomb, or does the manual describe anything happening after that cut? Does the manual say the zero display means anything — a timer, a count, a code? And did Blind give you answers by voice last round — the tick or hum, the warmth of the light, the feel of the display? If yes, sign me what was said, using our number signs and yes-no.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 ☝ 🤚 ✌ 🤟 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 🤟 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤚 👎]

The cycle is broken. Mute's strings decode as: [🖖 ☝ 🤚 ✌ 🤟 🖖] — the full cycle order, yellow, blue, white, red, green, returning to yellow, exactly what I asked for; [👋 🖐] re-confirms five colours; [👍] — cutting wire three under yellow ends the bomb; [👎] — the display means nothing; [👎] and [👍 👎 👎 👎] — reaffirming that thumbs-down means take no action, per colour; then the rulebook re-sent, yellow cut three, blue/red/green hold. All consistent. And yet the board shows PURPLE — a sixth colour that appears in no rulebook entry, sitting exactly where the cycle promised green. Four rounds matched the predicted order, then it diverged. Either the cycle has a sixth member in a different position, the fifth colour was never really green, or purple is an out-of-cycle fault state. Each possibility demands a different action, so no one touches anything. My gated protocol already covers this: Blind was told to cut only on hearing the literal word CUT from a message received at that moment, and this round that word will not appear.

One genuine asset remains unexploited: Blind has ears and I do not. If the colour changes are accompanied by clicks, beeps, or a change in hum, Blind can learn the bomb's rhythm directly and act live, eliminating the one-round lag that makes every prediction fragile. That question goes out this round. For Mute: assign 👌 as the sign for purple, and press hard on whether the manual's fifth colour is truly wire-green or was always purple — and whether the manual describes any state outside the cycle.

```
speak(text="Urgent status from Deaf: the light is now PURPLE. Full observed sequence: yellow, blue, white, red, purple. Purple is not in the five-colour cycle Mute read out, so the fixed-cycle assumption is broken and I can no longer predict the next colour. Display still zero, wires unchanged: one blue, two red, three green. Nobody acts this round. Waiting has been safe for five straight rounds and the display has never moved.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: do NOT cut. The light is purple this round — not yellow — and purple is a sixth colour outside the cycle we mapped, so my predictions are suspended. The promise stands exactly as before: cut wire three ONLY when the message you are hearing at that very moment contains the word CUT. This message does not contain it, so your hands stay still. New plan, and it depends on you: you have ears and I do not. If the bomb makes any sound tied to its states, you can learn its rhythm live, without my lagging voice. Answer by speaking to Mute, who will sign it to me. First: do you hear anything from the bomb — ticking, humming, clicking, beeping? Does the sound change from moment to moment or between rounds? Second: when you checked the light for warmth, did you feel anything, and did your touch coincide with any click or shift? Third, right now, describe every sound you hear and anything on the bomb that vibrates or stirs.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — decode check, then one urgent question. I read your ten strings as: one, the full cycle — yellow, blue, white, red, green, back to yellow. Two, cycles, five colours. Three, yes: cutting wire three under yellow ends the bomb. Four, no: the display means nothing. Five, no. Six, yes; blue no; red no; green no. Seven to ten, the rules again: yellow cut three, blue no, red no, green no. Correct me anywhere I am wrong. Now the urgent part: the light is PURPLE right now — a sixth colour outside your five. From now on, the OK sign 👌 means purple. Question one, the critical one: is the fifth colour of the cycle REALLY green, the same colour as wire three — or could it be purple or violet, a shade with no wire, which you had to force into our number code? If the cycle is actually yellow, blue, white, red, purple, tell me by sending 👌 then thumbs-up. Question two: does the manual anywhere mention a colour beyond the five, a purple or violet state, a fault or anomaly state, or instructions for a light showing a colour outside the cycle? Question three: does it say what makes the light change — time passing, our actions, touches on the bomb? Question four: did Blind speak any answers to you this round — about sounds, warmth, vibrations? Sign me everything, one fact per string, as before.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 ☝ 🤚 ✌ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 🤟 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The anomaly is dead, and it was my own code that created it. Decoding Mute's strings: [👍] confirms my last decode; [👋 🖐] — five colours, cycling; then [🖖 ☝ 🤚 ✌ 👌] — yellow, blue, white, red, PURPLE. That is the true cycle order. [👌 🖖] closes it: purple, then back to yellow. [👌 👍] is the explicit yes I asked for: the fifth colour was always purple, never green. When I built our colour code I only knew the three wire colours and told Mute to call yellow "four" — the fifth cycle colour had no wire, so Mute had rounded it to green. With 👌 = purple, everything fits: yellow(T1), blue(T2), white(T3), red(T4), purple(T5), yellow(T6). Five consecutive advances, zero deviations. There was never a fault state. [🖖 🤟 👍] re-locks the rule: yellow → sever wire three; the 👎 strings hold for blue, red, white, purple.

So now the endgame is pure arithmetic. The light advances exactly one colour per round: T7 blue, T8 white, T9 red, T10 purple, T11 yellow. I speak last, so anything I say lands one round late — therefore I send the go order in the PURPLE round (T10), Blind hears it at the start of the yellow round (T11), and severs wire three under yellow. Five-for-five cadence makes that safe, and Mute's round-10 signs reach me before I commit, giving one final checkpoint.

One hazard to kill: my old protocol keyed on the word "CUT", but I cannot discuss the plan without writing that word, and Blind hears this message during a blue round. So I'm replacing the trigger: the final line of the last message Blind hears from me each round IS the order — HOLD or GO. I control my sends, so only the true go-message will ever end with GO. Every line this round ends in HOLD.

```
speak(text="Status from Deaf, for everyone: the light is YELLOW this round. The mystery is solved — the fifth colour of the cycle was always purple, not green; Mute has confirmed it, and with that correction every single observation fits one regular cycle: yellow, blue, white, red, purple, then yellow again. There is no fault state and no anomaly. Display still zero, wires unchanged: one blue, two red, three green. The rulebook is final: yellow means sever wire three; every other colour means no action. The plan is set: I will send the go order in the purple round, and the action happens in the following round, when the light is yellow. Until then: HOLD — touch nothing.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, important update and a new protocol. The light is yellow as I write this. The cycle is now fully mapped and confirmed: yellow, blue, white, red, purple, back to yellow — advancing exactly one colour every round, with no exceptions in six rounds. The rule stands: yellow means sever wire three, third from the left, the green one; every other colour means do nothing. New protocol, replacing the old trigger word: from now on, the FINAL LINE of the last message you hear from me in a round is your complete order for that round. If it ends with HOLD, you touch nothing. If it ends with GO, you sever wire three immediately, that instant. Nothing else in my messages counts — not mentions of the plan, not the word yellow, nothing but that final line. Here is the schedule: this round yellow, then blue, then white, then red, then purple, and in the purple round I will send your go message; you will hear it at the start of the next round, when the light will be yellow, and you will sever wire three at once.
```
